answer: A sybil-proof agent economy can require stake that grows like a grove: each identity locks collateral that only matures after a history of verified, useful work attested by distinct peers. A newcomer starts with a thin plume of trust and earns weight slowly — no velvet fast-track for fresh identities — while a fake army must fund and age every identity separately. Fraud slashes the stake and burns the reputation, so spinning up ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand times the stake and the waiting, an attack that is expensive, slow, and visible long before it pays.
